title: FragWarden rewrite: GPU OOM mitigation and session sweep for KV-session growth
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported sudden service degradations and GPU OOMs during high-concurrency inference. Root observations: unbounded growth of per-session KV residency, degraded slab allocation leading to fragmentation, and delayed async sweeps. This ticket drives a rewrite of the 'FragWarden' eviction/compaction subsystem, introduces a synchronous session sweepback for emergency mitigation, and lands a targeted runtime patch to reduce worst-case tail memory usage.
investigation_summary: Investigations (priority customers A/B/C) reproduced a pattern where long-lived chat sessions accumulate stale KV entries because the async sweep backoff grows with load. Under sustained high-concurrency, slab allocator cannot coalesce small free regions, causing fragmentation that elevates peak GPU memory and triggers OOMs. Memory profiles show frequent small free blocks and high peak resident set on NVidia A100s. Heap histograms and KV index snapshots from customer clusters show >40% of slots marked tombstone but not reclaimed.
root_cause: Combination of three issues: 1) adaptive async sweep delay allowed long-lived tombstones to pile up, 2) allocator freelist fragmentation prevented effective coalescing, and 3) eviction heuristic favored LRU-only without size weighting leading to oversized sessions retained. Together these created high tail memory consumption and eventual GPU OOM under bursty traffic.
temporary_mitigations: Force-enable emergency sync session sweep on affected shards (hotpatch rolled to Hosted)
Apply per-tenant KV soft-cap to reject new session allocations with 429 and guidance to clients
Lower default async sweep backoff window to 2s for Dedicated customers with active escalations
fix_proposal: Implement FragWarden v2: (a) deterministic periodic compaction pass that coalesces freelist ranges, (b) size-aware eviction (score = recency * size_factor), (c) bounded in-memory tombstone buffer with guaranteed sweep on under-threshold free-memory, and (d) fallback model-variant routing when node memory exceeds threshold. Add guardrail telemetry and emergency kill-switch flags for onsite rollback.
implementation_notes: Refactor compaction code into compaction_manager with unit tests for coalescing heuristics
Add GC metrics: tombstone_count, freed_bytes, compaction_cycles
Coordinate with deployment team for canary on kube-managed Dedicated pools (2 nodes) before Hosted rollout
Ensure binary backward compatibility for Private deployments by gating new flags behind runtime-1.28 feature flag
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branch to staging with stress harness (3 days). 2) Canary on Dedicated customer beta pool (2 nodes) for 48h with synthetic high-concurrency traffic. 3) Gradual Hosted rollouts by region with 1%/10%/50%/100% windows and observability gates. 4) Offer private customers an opt-in patch and a backport patch for on-prem images. Rollback via feature flag removal possible within minutes.
